title: Associations between gestational exposure to perfluoroalkyl substances, fetal growth, and the mediation effect of thyroid hormones.
ehr_evidence: We enrolled 374 mother-infant pairs from the Ezhou birth cohort study between 2019 and 2020; PFASs and thyroid hormones were measured in maternal serum during the first trimester, and birth outcomes were obtained from the participants' medical records.
summary: A prospective birth cohort study of 379 mother-infant pairs in Ezhou City, China (2019-2020) examining associations between first-trimester maternal serum PFAS concentrations and birth outcomes (birth weight, length, head circumference, gestational age), with maternal thyroid hormones as mediators.
key_findings: Increasing PFNA (β = -0.54 cm, 95% CI: -0.90, -0.18) and PFHxS (β = -0.64 cm, 95% CI: -0.86, -0.42) concentrations were negatively associated with birth length.
Increasing PFOA (β = -0.73 cm, 95% CI: -1.19, -0.27) and PFHpS (β = -0.30 cm, 95% CI: -0.53, -0.07) concentrations were negatively associated with head circumference.
Each Ln increase in PFOA was associated with a 43.2 g decrease in birth weight (95% CI: -75.8, -10.6).
Each Ln increase in PFDA was negatively associated with gestational age (β = -0.18 week, 95% CI: -0.26, -0.10).
Maternal FT3 mediated 36.7% of the effect of PFNA on birth length, and FT4 mediated 30.8% of the effect of PFOA on head circumference.
No significant mediation by thyroid hormones was observed for birth weight or gestational age.
PFOS and PFNA were negatively associated with TSH, and PFDA was positively associated with TT4.
captured_features: maternal serum PFAS concentrations (PFOA, PFOS, PFNA, PFDA, PFHxS, PFOSA, PFHpS, PFHpA)
maternal thyroid hormone levels (TSH, FT3, FT4, TT4, TT3, TG)
maternal age, pre-pregnancy BMI, gestational weight gain, living area, maternal education, family income, parity, method of delivery, maternal occupation, second-hand smoke exposure
pathologies_diseases: Adverse fetal growth outcomes (reduced birth length, head circumference, birth weight, and gestational age)
study_design: Prospective birth cohort study (with cross-sectional assessment of PFAS-thyroid hormone associations and mediation analysis)
population: 379 mother-infant pairs from the Ezhou birth cohort in Ezhou City, Hubei, China; pregnant women recruited in early/first-trimester pregnancy (mean maternal age 27.3 years) with their live-born infants
exposure_domain: Perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) - environmental persistent chemicals
limitations: PFAS-thyroid hormone associations are cross-sectional, limiting causal inference.
First-trimester single measurements may lead to exposure misclassification.
Only 8 of at least 23 detectable PFASs were measured, possibly underestimating PFAS effects.
Participants from a single city in China, limiting generalizability to other countries and socioeconomic groups.
data_availability_statement: The datasets used and/or analysed during the current study available from the corresponding author on reasonable request.
